why: A (universe 0) is the item's only theorem PathSp.edist_toPathC_le: for ANY set N ⊆ V, the uniform distance in C([0,1],V) for the NORM of V between toPathC γ, toPathC γ' is ≤ Milnor's d (pathCSet, PathC, toPathC, pathIncl are vocabulary). B: on every abstract connected Hausdorff ℝⁿ-manifold with a smooth metric, (1) the compact-open topology of Ω* equals the topology generated by the balls of d* = max_t ρ (ρ the intrinsic distance), and (2) there is a continuous natural i : Ω → Ω* with d*(i w, i w') ≤ d(w, w'). B ⇒ A holds only vacuously: A is provable outright (A_outright: ‖γ(t)−γ'(t)‖ ≤ ρ ≤ supDist ≤ d, the project's own three lemmas). A ⇒ B fails genuinely: setting (abstract vs N ⊆ V), A's d* is the extrinsic norm distance not max ρ, and A lacks clause (1) altogether. On embedded manifolds A ⇒ B_emb is proved (A gives the continuity of i; clause (1) comes from ρ's continuity outside A).
overlap: B_to_A (= A_outright, hypothesis unused): 58 shared project theorems — the lemmas of A's own proof (supDist_le_edist, riemDist_le_supDist, ofReal_norm_sub_le_riemDist) and the proof fields of PathSp.instPseudoEMetricSpace / piecewise-smooth length lemmas behind them, i.e. the project's proof re-run. A_to_B_emb: 57 shared — the pseudo-emetric instance fields (supDist/l2Dist symmetry and triangle, Minkowski), riemDist_self/comm/triangle, ofReal_norm_sub_le_riemDist, riemDist_le_supDist, piecewise-smooth/pathLength lemmas used by the metric dictionary; edist_toPathC_le itself only enters through the hypothesis.
embedded_special_case_note: Items/V10_15.lean: B_emb := B for M = Bridge.Sub hN (↥N, model ℝⁿ, induced metric, ConnectedSpace) (B_to_B_emb). A_to_B_emb (#rt_check OK): clause (2): i := σ⁻¹ ∘ toPathC ∘ τ, continuous because A makes toPathC 1-Lipschitz; NatMap by rfl; d* ≤ d is immediate from the blind definitions (d = max_t ρ + L²-term). Clause (1) is NOT from A: Emb.topology_eq proves compact-open = d*-topology on ↥N from Morse.continuous_riemDist + riemDist_ne_top (ρ continuous and finite on connected N, so w' ↦ d*(w,w') is continuous by IsCompact.continuous_sSup) and ‖x−y‖ ≤ ρ(x,y) (uniform V-balls contain d*-balls).
